q: Stuck-Zimmer theorem (1994) concerns invariant random subgroups (IRS) of higher-rank lattices. An IRS of G is a conjugation-invariant probability measure on the space of closed subgroups Sub(G). Stuck-Zimmer showed that for higher-rank lattices Γ:
opts: Every ergodic IRS is either a fixed subgroup (Dirac mass on a normal subgroup) or the Haar measure on Γ\G (counting measure on conjugates of the trivial subgroup)
IRSs classify all subgroups of Γ
Every IRS is supported on amenable subgroups
exp: Stuck-Zimmer: for lattices in higher-rank simple Lie groups, every ergodic IRS (invariant random subgroup) is either supported on a fixed normal subgroup of finite index, or is the uniform measure on an orbit Γ/Λ for a lattice Λ. This 'classification of IRSs' is a far-reaching generalisation of Margulis's normal subgroup theorem.
